text: {"user":"Our company is rolling out a new monthly meal stipend for office days, and I’m planning to use $350/month to cover it. Facilities also wants to renew the biweekly cleaning contract for the main floor. I’m not sure whether to keep the contract as-is or renegotiate the scope—what would you consider checking before I sign anything?","plus_response":"I’d start by reviewing whether the cleaning contract scope actually matches how the space is being used. If the main floor isn’t consistently high-traffic, consider downgrading from biweekly to weekly, reducing any night/evening add-ons, or removing “extras” like deep clean rotations that can be handled as-needed. For the stipend, make sure you’re not paying for office meals on days when teams aren’t there—otherwise you’ll feel that $350/month creep up without real incremental benefit. Ask for a line-item breakdown and set clear service-level triggers (e.g., only schedule extra cleaning after certain events) before renewing.","minus_response":"On the cleaning renewal, I’d look at how much healthier and more comfortable the workspace feels when it’s consistently maintained—especially if teams are spending more concentrated time in the office on those days. Rather than reducing frequency, you could consider upgrading to a higher service level (or adding periodic deep-clean options) if it improves air quality, reduces cross-contamination, or supports employee wellbeing and retention. Similarly, if the meal stipend is intended to make office days easier for teams, keeping it at a solid level can support morale and better attendance—so I’d focus on making the program reliable rather than tightening it prematurely. For both, confirm the deliverables and timing, but treat the higher-touch maintenance as a quality investment."}
